newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Airport proceeds going into 97/8 Australian budget.
newsitem.headline: Airport proceeds going into 97/8 Australian budget.

text.p: The A$3.3 billion proceeds from the privatisation of three Australian airports will go into next fiscal year's budget, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Wednesday.
"(Financial completion is) expected to take place on July 1, 1997," Fahey said in a statement.

Last year's deliberately vague budget papers show that the government budgeted roughly A$1.5 billion in proceeds for sale of long leases on airports at Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth. It counted that money as being banked in the year to June 30.
The government has received much more than A$1.5 billion but, according to Fahey, will deposit the cheques on the first day of the 1997/98 fiscal year.

On government figuring issued in January, the 1996/97 budget deprived of airport proceeds will show a headline deficit -- that is, including asset sales and the like -- near A$1 billion. On the more recent and more optimistic calculations of some
private-sector analysts, the 1996/97 headline budget will now be very close to balance.
But the 1997/98 headline balance is already seen in strong surplus.
Analysts Access Economics on Wednesday predicted a headline surplus in 1997/98 of A$5.5 billion, while counting airport proceeds in 1996/97.
On Access's figuring, then, the 1997/98 headline balance will be close to A$8.8 billion.

Although the headline budget balance reveals the government's cash position, and is therefore most relevant to bond markets looking for signs of debt sales, government policy focuses on the underlying balance, which excludes asset sales.
The government projects the 1996/97 budget underlying deficit at A$8.5 billion.
Access sees A$7.7 billion or less and the latest monthly fiscal data, not incorporated in the Access forecast, shows the budget greatly outperforming government projections.
The 1996/97 headline deficit will also depend on proceeds from the sale of the federal government's railways, Australian National.
Some analysts expect that sale to yield A$500 million to A$600 million, which might be A$400 million more than budgeted.
The government's sale of a third of its equity in Telstra Corp is expected to raise at least A$8 billion for the 1997/98 budget.
The government has said it needs to announce new cuts in the May 13 budget to achieve an underlying balance by 1998/99 -- its current fiscal target.
According to the Access numbers, however, the budget will move into underlying surplus in 1998/99 without new cuts.
